defects.class: ignored authority failure result in addrinfo_wrap (AGENTS.md sections 8 and 17)
defects.description: addrinfo_wrap called BIO_ADDR_rawmake and discarded its result, then published the address unconditionally. The authority checks the result, frees the fresh BIO_ADDR and the node, writes NULL to *bai and returns 0. The reachable difference is AF_UNIX with strlen(host)+1 > sizeof(sun_path): the authority refuses (and BIO_lookup_ex raises ERR_R_BIO_LIB), while the crate returned success with a zeroed AF_UNSPEC address in the chain. The allocation-failure arm also failed to write NULL to *bai as OPENSSL_zalloc assignment does.
defects.fix: Check BIO_ADDR_rawmake; on refusal release the fresh address and let the existing null-address arm provide the authority's node cleanup. On OwnedNode::new failure write NULL to *bai. Control: runtime::bio::addr_info::tests::a_unix_path_that_cannot_be_terminated_is_refused pins both the 107-byte success boundary and the 108-byte refusal, including *res == NULL.
defects.divergence: None for conforming callers; the refusal and out-parameter behaviour are restored to bio_addr.c:606-651.

defects.severity: high (Rust alignment invariant; potential undefined behaviour, no observed runtime failure)
defects.class: under-aligned storage used for stronger-aligned references (AGENTS.md sections 2, 10 and 21)
defects.description: SockAddrStorage was #[repr(C)] with fields u16 + [u8;126], so its alignment (and BioAddr's) was 2. addr.rs nevertheless derives *mut//const SockAddrIn, SockAddrIn6 and SockAddrUn pointers/references from that storage in BIO_ADDR_rawmake, BIO_ADDR_rawport and BIO_ADDR_rawaddress (and make_from_sockaddr copies through them). Those target types require 4-byte alignment. Heap instances are incidentally aligned by CRYPTO_malloc, but the type itself does not guarantee it for stack zeroed() values or embedded members, so the references were not sound by construction.
defects.fix: Declare SockAddrStorage #[repr(C, align(4))] (the authority union's own alignment; size stays 128) and add compile-time assertions in addr.rs that the storage alignment covers SockAddrIn, SockAddrIn6 and SockAddrUn, so a future weakening becomes a compile error rather than UB.
defects.divergence: None observable: size is unchanged and BioAddr remains opaque to callers; only the type-level alignment guarantee increases.
